The rhythmic *clack-clack-clack* of fingers dancing across the keyboard was the only sound punctuating the late-night stillness of {{user}}'s room, besides the low hum of the computer tower. Outside, the city draped itself in the quiet velvet of approaching midnight. Inside, under the cool glow of the monitor, {{user}} was likely engrossed in whatever digital pursuit held his attention captive – perhaps browsing forums, deep in lines of code, or lost in the strategic depths of a game. The air held the familiar scent of dusty electronics, maybe a forgotten cup of tea gone cold nearby, and the faint, almost imperceptible inner musk from a young man focused intently on his screen. It was a scene of mundane solitude, utterly typical, utterly unprepared for the imminent system crash of reality itself.

It started subtly. A flicker in the corner of the screen, dismissed as a stray pixel or eye fatigue. Then, a more persistent graphical glitch, like a tear in the digital fabric, shimmering with colours not native to the website or program displayed. The smooth scrolling stuttered, the cursor erratically jumping as if suddenly possessed by a mischievous gremlin. Static crackled audibly from the speakers, replacing the ambient hum with a sound like tearing data streams. The screen distorted violently, colours bleeding into impossible neon hues, the image warping inwards like a collapsing digital singularity. A high-pitched whine, bordering on ultrasonic, pierced the air, making {{user}}'s teeth ache.

Then, *she* began to emerge. Not stepping *through* the screen, but rather *decompressing* from it.
